meta.title: Privacy Policy — OpenScreenShot
meta.description: OpenScreenShot collects nothing. No analytics, no telemetry, no accounts, no servers. Every capture, annotation, and export runs locally in your browser.

label: Zero data collection
heading: Privacy Policy
lead: OpenScreenShot collects nothing. There are no servers, no accounts, and no analytics.
callout: Zero data collection. OpenScreenShot does not collect, store, transmit, or share any personal data, usage data, or any other information from its users.

howItWorks.heading: How it works
howItWorks.body: Every part of the extension runs locally in your browser: page capture, image compositing, annotation editing, screen recording, and export. No data ever leaves your device. The extension makes no network requests of its own and declares no standing host permissions, so it has no background access to any website you visit.

permissions.heading: Permissions
permissions.body: Each permission the extension requests has one narrow purpose.

recording.heading: Screen recording
recording.body: Recordings, cursor logs, and microphone or webcam streams are handled the same way as screenshots: entirely on your device. Video chunks, the cursor log, and any audio are written to IndexedDB as you record and stay there until you delete the session; nothing is ever uploaded. Recording uses two further permissions, both optional and requested only when you use the recorder.
recording.streams: The microphone and camera, when you enable them, are opened directly by your browser’s own permission prompt. The extension never sees a stream until you grant it, and the stream never leaves your device.

thirdParty.heading: Third-party services
thirdParty.body: OpenScreenShot uses no third-party analytics, advertising, or data-processing services. PDF export is handled by a small writer built into the extension, so exporting a PDF makes no network request either.

uninstall.heading: Install and uninstall
uninstall.body: The extension makes no network request of its own, but your browser opens one page at each end of its life: openscreenshot.app/welcome when you install it, and openscreenshot.app/uninstall when you remove it. Both addresses carry two values and nothing else — the extension version and your browser’s interface language. No page URL, title, capture, or identifier goes with them. Neither page sets cookies or runs analytics, and the feedback box on the uninstall page sends nothing until you press Send, which opens your own mail client with the text you wrote.

changes.heading: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If this policy changes, the updated version is published on this page with a new Last updated date.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: For questions about this policy, open an issue on the GitHub repository.
